texts: On day 85 of Year 1, the lanterns at the Hollows drew many nightmoths.
The lanterns of the Cliff Path drew a handful of nightmoths that autumn.
A handful of sky-cats hunted on the Cliff Path that autumn, so a handful of nightmoths fled to the Hollows.
Pell wrote a note about the Hollows for the Council.
The thread harvest at the Hollows rose in that week.
The thread harvest on the Cliff Path stayed thin in that week.

sentences: On day 85 of Year 1, the lanterns at the Hollows drew many nightmoths.

q1_issues.issue: The per-member rule hands every individual lantern the whole existential moth group as Theme ((Theme (sk_draw $x) sk_nightmoth_1)), asserting that each lantern drew all the many nightmoths rather than that the lanterns drew them between them.
Same over-distribution: each lantern of the Cliff Path is made to draw the entire handful sk_nightmoth_2.

Sentence 3's vague-quantity plurals ("a handful of sky-cats hunted", "a handful of nightmoths fled") get group events with no per-member distribution rule, although hunt and flee are distributive and the same construction got rules at 12 and 25.

"in that week" is encoded as the bare constant that_week, an anaphoric NP treated as a speech-anchored deictic; it also propagates nothing, unlike "that autumn" at 23-24 and 33-34, which did copy (Year 1).

q2_gaps: Anaphoric temporal NPs coarser than a day ("that autumn", "in that week"): term propagation is specified for day-level terms plus a day-part symbol, so a season or a week has no defined filler, and when the antecedent supplies no term at that level there is nothing to copy.
Day-of-year dating in a fictional calendar ("On day 85 of Year 1"): (Day n) is defined as a calendar day inside a month/date, not a day ordinal within a year.

A counted/vague-quantity object group under a distributed subject ("the lanterns drew many nightmoths"): the distribution machinery specifies a shared definite object, and nothing says whether such an object should become a Skolem group per member or block the rule.
review.notes: "the Hollows" (capitalized plural label -> Name-only individual, no GroupOf/type), "the Council" (capitalized common noun -> common-noun default, no Name), "on the Cliff Path" as an entity-attached surface preposition against "at the Hollows" as LocatedIn, the scalar-change Theme on rise, and the stayed-thin continuation-copular bundle (Still + flat + tense) all match the instruction set precisely. The defects are confined to the distribution rules and the anaphoric time NPs.

issues.reason: The rule hands every member the same constant object group, asserting that each lantern drew all the many nightmoths -- more than the text states -- and Quantifiers, generics & scope fixes the opposite form for a count under a distributed subject (a per-binding Skolem group, a shared constant only on a 'the same' cue).
Same over-assertion on the same rule form: (Theme (sk_draw $x) sk_nightmoth_2) makes each Cliff Path lantern draw the entire handful, which the sentence does not say.

Cardinality states that a counted/vague-quantity plural with a distributive predicate keeps the group event and count and adds the per-member rule over (PartOf $x <group>); hunt and flee are distributive, so omitting the rule drops an atom the instruction set requires (and the same parse emitted it twice for draw).

The propagation half stands -- 'in that week' is an anaphoric temporal NP, and term propagation requires copying the antecedent's stated terms, here (Year 1), exactly as the parse did for 'that autumn' -- but the deictic-constant complaint is overstated, since Time's term inventory has no week-level term and a bare symbol is the nearest licensed shape in that gap.

gaps_confirmed: Anaphoric temporal NPs coarser than a day ('that autumn', 'in that week'): term propagation is defined over day-level calendar terms plus a day-part symbol, so a season or a week has no defined Time filler.
Day-of-year dating in a fictional calendar ('day 85 of Year 1'): (Day n) is a calendar day inside a month/date, not a day ordinal within a year.

A counted/vague-quantity object group under a distributed plural subject ('the lanterns drew many nightmoths'): the distribution machinery covers a shared definite object only, and says nothing about whether such an object becomes a per-member Skolem group or blocks the rule.
new_gaps: Cumulative counted object under a distributed subject: neither licensed form is faithful -- a shared constant object gives every member the whole set, and the per-binding Skolem group ((sk_moth $x) with its own CardinalityPhrase) gives every member 'many' of its own -- so a licensed form would need to carry that the count is a total over the group while the predication still reaches individual members.
adjudication.defect_summary: Issues 0 and 1: the object must not be a shared constant inside the per-member rule -- the nearest licensed form is a per-binding Skolem group, (Theme (sk_draw $x) (sk_moth $x)) + (GroupOf (sk_moth $x) nightmoth), but since the counts 'many'/'a handful' are cumulative over the lanterns no licensed form carries them faithfully, so the compliant minimum is the group event alone with no per-member rule (filed as a gap). Issue 2: emit the per-member rules the instruction set mandates -- (Implication (PartOf $x sk_skycat_1) (And (Member (sk_hunt $x) hunt) (Agent (sk_hunt $x) $x) (Location (sk_hunt $x) cliff_path) (Past (sk_hunt $x)) ...)) and the matching flee rule over sk_nightmoth_3.
adjudication.notes: The reviewer's positive reading is right: the Hollows name-only individual, the Council common-noun default, LocatedIn for 'at' against the entity-attached On for 'on', the So connective in surface order, the scalar-change Theme, and the stayed-thin Still/flat/tense bundle all follow the instruction set. The defects are the distribution rules on both sides -- two emitted that over-assert and two omitted that were required.
